column3: “Holds” renders “has”; “a reputation for being alive” renders “a name that you are alive.”
“Wake up” renders “be watching”; “incomplete” renders “not completed.”
BSB follows the critical text with “I will come like a thief” (no “upon you”).
“Because they are worthy” is moved forward; “people” renders ὀνόματα (“names”).
“Like them” renders οὕτως (“thus”); “but” is added.
Close to the Greek.
“The One who is holy and true” recasts “the Holy One, the True One.” BSB has no “except the one who opens” (εἴ …).
Close to the Greek.
“Look at those who belong to” recasts “behold, I give [those] of”; “are liars instead” renders “they lie.” “I love you” renders the aorist “I loved you.”
“My command to persevere” renders “the word of My patient endurance”; “testing” renders “trial.”
BSB follows the critical text with no “Behold.”
BSB puts “the new Jerusalem … from My God” in parentheses.
Close to the Greek.
“Originator” renders ἀρχὴ (“beginning”).
“How I wish you were one or the other!” recasts “I wish you were cold or hot.”
“Vomit” renders ἐμέσαι (“spit out”).
“Pitiful” renders “miserable”; “realize” renders “know.”
BSB follows the critical text with “salve to anoint your eyes.” “Your shameful nakedness” renders “the shame of your nakedness.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
“Grant the right to sit” renders “give to sit.”
Close to the Greek.
